title: The Mountain of Truth and What It Cost: Antwerp, Ascona, and the Brazilian sequels
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Antwerp, and the Cure at Veldes

stops.name: Antwerp, born into an industrial house
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year and the city only. HDS (hls-dhs-dss.ch, article 049204, by Andreas Schwab, 2009) and de.wikipedia both give 1875 Antwerp with no day or month, and no civil record was reached. The pin is the Cathedral of Our Lady, the city's landmark, and is not a documented birth site; coordinates corrected to 51.2206, 4.4006
stops.campa: A son is born in Antwerp to a rich industrial house, and the record keeps almost nothing else: no day, no month, no street, only the year and the city. Of the twenty-four years between this entry and the next one that survives, nothing at all is known. The Swiss dictionary that will one day file him calls him a Belgian merchant of no confession, son of a wealthy Antwerp industrialist. The port outside is thick with grain, diamonds and colonial freight, and the family money sits somewhere inside that traffic.
suggested_refs: Antwerp civil registers for 1875, unconsulted; no birth act for Oedenkoven located in any reachable source
sources: hls-dhs-dss.ch/fr/articles/049204/ (Historical Dictionary of Switzerland, Andreas Schwab, 2009)

stops.name: Borgerhout, the grandfather's name and money
stops.date_confidence: the grandfather's mayoralty of Borgerhout and his guardianship of Georges Eekhoud are attested (nl.wikipedia, 'Georges Eekhoud'); the candle factory is not, and no firm, trade register or ownership share was located. The date 1885 orders the segment and is not a record of the boy at this address
stops.campa: He carries his grandfather's name. The elder Henri Oedenkoven, dead four years before the boy is born, was an industrialist and former mayor of Borgerhout, then a municipality in its own right on Antwerp's eastern edge, and guardian to his orphaned nephew, the writer Georges Eekhoud, who grew up in his house. The money the grandson will spend on a hillside in Switzerland is old enough by then to be inherited rather than earned. Belgian writing puts a candle factory behind the fortune; no trade register or company record was located to confirm it.
stops.quote: Zijn voogd werd daarna zijn oom Henri Oedenkoven (overleden in 1871), industrieel en oud-burgemeester van Borgerhout.
stops.quote_source: nl.wikipedia, 'Georges Eekhoud', on the subject's grandfather and namesake
suggested_refs: Belgian trade-register and company records for the Oedenkoven firm at Borgerhout, not located

stops.name: Veldes, the cure at Rikli's institute
stops.date_confidence: attested to the summer of 1899 by Hofmann's 1906 memoir and by HDS 049204; the month is a placeholder within that summer. The pin is the corpus's canonical Veldes coordinate, and the exact footprint of Rikli's establishment is unlocated. The 'north shore' given in earlier compilation is unsupported: Straza hill and the surviving Vila Rikli lie south of the water
stops.campa: Illness carries him, by his partner's later account, to the edge of the grave and back again by way of vegetarianism. He comes to Veldes on the lake the Slovenes call Bled, where Arnold Rikli has run a light, air and water institute since the 1850s. Barefoot walking at dawn, huts open on one side to the weather, cold baths, no meat: everything the Belgian will set up on a Ticinese hillside eighteen months from now is already running here, a generation early. Rikli put up a villa in the Swiss style in 1895 and added a swimming place and a promenade the year Oedenkoven arrives.
stops.quote: Krankheit bis zum Grabesrande führte ihn auf den Läuterungsweg des Vegetarismus.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verita. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (Lorch: Karl Rohm, 1906), p. 4, on Oedenkoven; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD, as quoted in the corpus file arnold_rikli / ida_hoffmann
suggested_refs: Arnold Rikli's Naturheilanstalt Mallnerbrunn at Veldes (Bled), and the surviving Vila Rikli

stops.name: Veldes, Ida Hofmann and Karl Graser
stops.date_confidence: attested to the same 1899 stay by Hofmann's memoir, which names him as the man who won her to the scheme; the month is a placeholder within that summer
stops.campa: Two others are taking the same cure. Ida Hofmann is a Viennese piano teacher eleven years his senior, at Veldes because her father is ill. Karl Graser is a former Habsburg officer from Transylvania who has thrown up his commission and means never to own anything again. In the huts and along the shore the three of them settle on a plan: a cooperative settlement somewhere south, where the sun holds all year and land can be bought outright. Hofmann's memoir names the season, the institute, and the man who won her to it.
stops.quote: Im Sommer 1899, gelegentlich eines gemeinsamen Aufenthaltes in der Naturheilanstalt Rikli in Veldes gewann mich Henri Oedenkoven für das in grossen Zügen geschilderte Zukunftsunternehmen.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verita. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 4; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD. The scan reads 'gelegenthch'; normalized
suggested_refs: The Rikli cure huts at Veldes, where the founding trio first met

stops.name: Munich, the founding meeting
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1900 (en.wikipedia, 'Monte Verita'), which also calls the scheme presented there Oedenkoven's plan; the day and the meeting address are unrecorded and default to the first
stops.campa: In October the group constitutes itself in Munich: Oedenkoven and Hofmann, Karl Graser and his younger brother Gusto, Ida's sisters Jenny and Lilly, Lotte Hattemer from Berlin, Ferdinand Brune. The record calls the scheme laid before them Oedenkoven's plan. They agree to pool personal property into a vegetable cooperative and to buy land with it, and it is understood, without anyone writing it into the articles, whose property will do most of the pooling. Gusto Graser is twenty-one and already a wandering prophet. No site has been chosen.
suggested_refs: The October 1900 Munich founding meeting of the Monte Verita vegetable cooperative

stops.name: Munich, the free union
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed. de.wikipedia dates the Reformehe to 1900 and names no place; Munich is used because the group had not yet reached the Ticino that autumn, so the Monte Verita pin is impossible. In law this was a freie Ehe and not a marriage; the day is a placeholder
stops.campa: He and Hofmann declare themselves joined in what they call a Reformehe, a reform marriage, and also a vegetarian marriage. No priest is asked and no registry entered. The refusal is doctrine rather than convenience: they hold love to be a union completed freely in nature, and hold both the blessing and the state act to be impositions laid on it afterwards. The place is unrecorded, though the group had not yet reached the Ticino that autumn. Hofmann sets the position out in print six years later, in the first person plural, and signs the title page Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven.
stops.quote: Liebe, als eine in der Natur »frei« sich vollziehende Vereinigung zweier Wesen betrachtend, verwerfen wir für uns sowohl den priesterlichen Segensspruch als den Staatsakt.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verita. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 18; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD
suggested_refs: The Reformehe or vegetarische Ehe of Hofmann and Oedenkoven, 1900

stops.name: Oberammergau, the road south
stops.date_confidence: attested only that six young founders travelled through northern Italy and southern Switzerland in autumn 1900 (aboutswitzerland.eda.admin.ch). The route through Oberammergau is the corpus's reconstruction from ida_hoffmann.journey.json, and the day is a placeholder
stops.campa: Six of them go south in the autumn looking for ground. Nothing has been bought and no site has been chosen. The road out of Bavaria runs through Oberammergau, where the season just ending has drawn crowds all summer, and where the villagers have staged the Passion every tenth year since a plague vow of 1634: a whole village organised around one collective promise kept for two and a half centuries. What is attested of the founders is only that they crossed northern Italy and southern Switzerland that autumn. The road through this village is reconstruction.
suggested_refs: The Oberammergau Passion season of 1900, the last before the founders' journey south

stops.name: Cadenabbia, the lakes
stops.date_confidence: route reconstruction from ida_hoffmann.journey.json; no independently fetched source names a stopping town between Munich and Ascona. The day is a placeholder
stops.campa: They come down onto the Italian lakes and stop at Cadenabbia on the western shore of Como, in the belt of villas and lemon terraces where northern Europeans have wintered for a century because the water holds the heat. This is the climate the plan requires: sun through the winter, water to look at, a hillside cheap enough to buy outright. Como is none of the last. They go on west and north toward the Swiss border and a poorer shore. No source reached names a stopping town between Munich and Ascona, and the halt here is reconstructed rather than recorded.
suggested_refs: The Lake Como villa belt at Cadenabbia, waypoint of the 1900 land search

stops.name: Ascona, the hill bought from Alfredo Pioda
stops.date_confidence: attested that the purchase from Alfredo Pioda took place in 1900 (en.wikipedia, 'Monte Verita'; aboutswitzerland.eda.admin.ch); month and day are placeholders. The price of 150,000 francs carried in earlier compilation is unsourced: the Canton Ticino page cited for it was fetched and carries only the line 'Dal Belgio il primo proprietario del Monte Verita di Ascona'. The pin is the corpus's canonical Monte Verita coordinate; survey gives the hill as 46.1589, 8.7629
stops.campa: Above the fishing village of Ascona on Lake Maggiore stands Monte Monescia, a poor hill of overgrown terraces belonging to Alfredo Pioda, a Ticinese politician and theosophist who had announced a lay monastery there called Fraternitas and never built it. Oedenkoven buys the ground. The enterprise is a cooperative in its articles and the deed is in his name, bought with Belgian family money. The price of a hundred and fifty thousand francs, carried in earlier compilation, is not supported by the cantonal page cited for it, which gives one line: from Belgium, the first owner of the Monte Verita of Ascona.
suggested_refs: Alfredo Pioda's unbuilt theosophical Fraternitas project on Monte Monescia
sources: www4.ti.ch/can/oltreconfiniti (fetched; one-line entry only, does not support the price)

stops.name: Monte Verita, the light-air huts
stops.date_confidence: attested to the settlement's first period (aboutswitzerland.eda.admin.ch; corpus ida_hoffmann.journey.json); no month or day recorded, and the date orders the segment
stops.campa: The first winter goes on clearing terraces that have grown over and putting up timber huts open on one side to the air. There is no hotel, no plumbing and no staff. Members dig, carry, plant fruit trees and eat what the ground gives them, which in the first year is not much. Oedenkoven, who has never worked with his hands for a living, works with them here beside a discharged cavalry officer and a Viennese piano teacher. The hill is still called Monescia. Nobody has thought of the other name yet.
suggested_refs: The first Luftbaracken or air huts of the Monte Verita cooperative, 1901

stops.name: Monte Verita, Gusto Graser put out
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1901 by the corpus files ida_hoffmann.journey.json and gusto_graeser.journey.json; no month or day recorded and the month is a placeholder
stops.campa: Within a year the settlement has guests, fees and a ledger. Gusto Graser, who owns nothing and intends to own nothing, will not accept payment as the basis of a shared life, and the man who bought the mountain puts him off it. The expulsion is dated to 1901 and to no month. He does not go far: he moves into a rock grotto below the meadow and stays there more than a decade, barefoot and long-haired, visible from the terraces, drawing pilgrims of his own up the hill past the sanatorium.
suggested_refs: Gusto Graser's grotto below the Monte Verita meadow, occupied from 1901

stops.name: Monte Verita, the cooperative splits
stops.date_confidence: attested to December 1901 by the corpus file karl_graser.journey.json; the day is a placeholder. The pin is Oedenkoven's own ground, not Karl Graser's adjoining plot, which the corpus pins separately at 46.153, 8.769
stops.campa: In December Karl Graser goes too, unwilling to live off paying guests, and settles on adjoining ground with Jenny Hofmann under a rule that nothing may be accepted from anyone. Oedenkoven keeps the deed, the name and the plan. The vegetable cooperative ends as a common purse and continues as an establishment, with a proprietor, a tariff and a doctrine attached to it. Three of the seven who signed at Munich fourteen months ago are now off the property, two of them on ground within sight of it.
suggested_refs: The adjoining plot above Ascona held by Karl Graser and Jenny Hofmann from December 1901

stops.name: Monte Verita, the first sun bath
stops.date_confidence: attested to mid-February 1902 from Hofmann's diary as relayed by aboutswitzerland.eda.admin.ch ('Mid-February 1902: First sun bath'); the fifteenth stands for the middle of the month
stops.campa: In the middle of February, with the lake below still cold, the first sun bath is taken on the terraces and Hofmann writes it into the diary. This is the therapy the whole enterprise rests on: skin to the light, no clothes, no meat, cold water, hours of open air. Rikli taught it at Veldes and Oedenkoven has carried it over the Alps and set it up as a going concern on a Ticinese hillside where the sun holds through the winter. It is one of the few dates from the first years fixed to a week.
suggested_refs: Ida Hofmann's diary of the first Monte Verita years, source of the February 1902 sun-bath entry

stops.name: Monte Verita, the name and the trade name
stops.date_confidence: attested to early spring 1902 for the naming (aboutswitzerland.eda.admin.ch) and to 1902 for the trading name Sanatorium Monte Verita (en.wikipedia, 'Monte Verita'); day and month are placeholders
stops.campa: In the early spring they rename the hill Monte Verita, mountain of truth, because the undertaking was founded by truth seekers. In the same year the establishment starts calling itself Sanatorium Monte Verita and advertising a vegetarian cure to the whole of Europe. The word chosen for a conviction is now also a trade name, printed on a letterhead. Letters come back from Berlin, Vienna, Amsterdam and Milan, asking after the terms, the season, the diet and the price per week.
stops.quote: because our undertaking was founded by truth seekers
stops.quote_source: The naming rationale as given in 'Monte Verita: The Swiss early hippie colony', aboutswitzerland.eda.admin.ch (Presence Switzerland), from Hofmann's account
suggested_refs: The 1902 prospectus of the Sanatorium Monte Verita

stops.name: Monte Verita, the statement of 1903
stops.date_confidence: attested as a 1903 statement of Oedenkoven's in the Fondazione Beatrice Trussardi essay 'Monte Verita', whose raw HTML was read directly; the essay carries no footnote to the original German pamphlet, which was not seen, so the underlying document is unverified. Month and day are placeholders
stops.campa: He writes for the public in the voice of a proprietor and not of a hermit. The settlement is no renunciation of the century, he insists, but a correct use of it: science, hygiene, machinery, running water, electric light off a stream bought for the purpose. The pitch is aimed squarely at the class he came from, people who can pay for a cure and who need telling that nothing here will be lacking. A few hundred metres away, on the adjoining plot, Karl Graser is going without on principle.
stops.quote: We make judicious use of all the tools made available by science and modern hygiene, we lack nothing.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Henri Oedenkoven, 1903, in the Fondazione Beatrice Trussardi essay 'Monte Verita' (beatricetrussardifoundation.com/ideas/3-monte-verita/), read in raw HTML; no footnote to the original German document is given there
suggested_refs: The 1903 promotional statement of the Sanatorium Monte Verita, original German printing not located

stops.name: Monte Verita, Casa Anatta
stops.date_confidence: disputed. The traditional date is 1904, with inauguration in 1905, but de.wikipedia, 'Casa Anatta', reports newer scholarship placing construction after 1907 or 1908, because the house appears in no earlier report or photograph. The architect is unknown; Oedenkoven is credited only with shaping the design, and earlier compilation's 'personally directed the building' is not reproduced. The pin is the corpus's canonical Casa Anatta coordinate
stops.campa: He builds a house for himself and Hofmann on the slope above the huts and calls it Casa Anatta, a Buddhist word for no-self. Rounded corners, double timber walls with air between them, sliding partitions, domed ceilings, windows opened wide onto the mountain and the lake. The architect is unrecorded; the design is his. It is at once the founders' residence and the room where guests are received: Mary Wigman dances in it, Martin Buber argues in it, Ida Hofmann plays Wagner in it, and Bebel and Kautsky sit in it talking politics.
stops.quote: a perfect example of liberated living
stops.quote_source: Sigfried Giedion on Casa Anatta, 1929, as quoted by Fondazione Monte Verita, monteverita.org/history. de.wikipedia, 'Casa Anatta', separately records Giedion calling it 'das originellste Holzhaus der Schweiz' in the Schweizerische Schreinerzeitung, 1934; both may be genuine
suggested_refs: Casa Anatta, Monte Verita, its double timber walls and sliding partitions
Sigfried Giedion's writings on Casa Anatta, 1929 and 1934

stops.name: Monte Verita, Casa Centrale
stops.date_confidence: the building, its yin-yang symbols and its planning for maximum natural light are attested (monteverita.org/history); no source reached gives a construction year, and 1904 orders the segment only. The claim in earlier compilation that Oedenkoven's friend Walter Hoffmann built it appears in no source reached and is not carried
stops.campa: The communal building goes up for dining, reading, music and assembly, planned for the greatest possible daylight, with yin and yang symbols worked into the windows and the balconies. The machinery is part of the argument, not a concession: with simple living and modern machines the house can be run without servants, and everyone in it can serve themselves. Water bought from a source nearby drives a small electrical plant. The sentence that states the principle carries no attribution and no date in the essay that prints it, and the speaker is inferred.
stops.quote: We want everyone, without having to leave the area, to be able to have everything they want at their fingertips, without the help of servants. Given the simplicity of our way of life and with the help of modern machinery capable of producing everything, everyone will be able to provide for themselves.
stops.quote_source: Unattributed quotation in the Fondazione Beatrice Trussardi essay 'Monte Verita' (beatricetrussardifoundation.com), following but not continuous with the 1903 Oedenkoven statement: an authorial sentence intervenes and the passage carries no attribution tag and no date, so the speaker is inferred from the nearest preceding attribution
suggested_refs: Casa Centrale, Monte Verita, with the yin-yang motifs in its windows and balconies

stops.name: Bayreuth, the Festspielhaus
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The Bayreuth visit and the meeting with Isadora Duncan on 13 August 1904 derive from Ida Hofmann's memoir tradition as relayed in earlier compilation; no independent contemporary record was reached. Coordinates corrected to the Festspielhaus at 49.9600, 11.5797, about 1.6 km from the figure carried previously
stops.campa: They travel north in August to the Green Hill, where Richard Wagner's theatre buries the orchestra under the stage and blacks out the house so that nothing is visible but the drama. Hofmann plays Wagner on the piano in Ticino; here they hear him staged as he wanted him staged. Her memoir puts a meeting with Isadora Duncan at Bayreuth on the thirteenth of August, the dancer who has already thrown off the corset and the shoe for much the same reasons the sanatorium throws off wool and cooked meat. No contemporary record of the meeting has been found.
suggested_refs: The Bayreuth Festspielhaus, sunken orchestra pit and darkened auditorium
Ida Hofmann's memoir account of the 1904 Bayreuth journey

stops.name: Monte Verita, the cure in print
stops.date_confidence: the brochure text is verbatim from ymago.net, which does not disambiguate whether the wording is Oedenkoven's or Ida Hofmann's, whose 1905 pamphlet is cited nearby: it is an unsigned institutional brochure. The 1905 Provisorische Statuten are attested only through later quotation, with no surviving printing, edition, translation or library holding located anywhere. Month and day are placeholders
stops.campa: The house issues brochures. The vegetarian cure, one of them explains, starts from what every method of healing starts from: that a body still able to live holds force enough in itself to bring about its own recovery, provided it is allowed to live according to the laws of nature. In the same year Oedenkoven draws up provisional statutes for the vegetarian society of Monte Verita. It is the one text most securely his own, and no copy of it has been located in any catalogue.
stops.quote: Comme toutes les autres méthodes de guérison, la cure végétarienne part du principe qu'un organisme, dans la mesure où il est capable de vivre, possède en lui-même suffisamment de force pour induire sa propre guérison, à condition qu'il lui soit permis de vivre en accord avec les lois de la nature.
stops.quote_source: Monte Verita promotional brochure, quoted in French translation on ymago.net (photo/monteverita/mystique.html), footnote 12, citing R. Landmann, Monte Verita, Die Geschichte eines Berges (Berlin: Adalbert Schultz Verlag, 1930), p. 151. Apostrophes normalized to straight; accents as in the source
suggested_refs: Henri Oedenkoven, Provisorische Statuten der vegetarischen Gesellschaft Monte Verita (1905), no surviving printing located
Robert Landmann, Monte Verita, Die Geschichte eines Berges (Berlin, 1930), p. 151
sources: literaturkritik.de/id/6486 (review of Andreas Schwab, Monte Verita: Sanatorium der Sehnsucht, 2003)

stops.name: Monte Verita, Muhsam's verdict
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1905 for Muhsam's stay and for the Locarno pamphlet (corpus erich_muhsam.journey.json; literaturkritik.de/id/6486); the month is a placeholder
stops.campa: Erich Muhsam climbs up, stays, and publishes at Locarno the first sustained insider account of the place. What he finds is not a commune but an establishment: a hotel pension with an ethical signboard, a sanatorium like any other, run on tariffs. What he admires instead is the ragged practice of Karl Graser on the next plot, who takes nothing from anyone and charges nobody. The house will go on paying its way for another fifteen years. Whether Oedenkoven ever answered the pamphlet is not recorded in any source reached.
stops.quote_source: Erich Muhsam on Monte Verita, 1905, quoted in the literaturkritik.de review (id/6486) of Andreas Schwab, Monte Verita: Sanatorium der Sehnsucht (Orell Fussli, 2003); Muhsam adds 'ein Sanatorium wie andere auch'
suggested_refs: Erich Muhsam, Ascona (Locarno, 1905), the first insider account of the colony

stops.name: Ascona, the death of Lotte Hattemer
stops.date_confidence: attested to 19 April 1906 (corpus ida_hoffmann.journey.json; de.wikipedia, 'Lotte Hattemer'). The rumour implicating a colony physician is reported, never adjudicated, and no source reached names a finding
stops.campa: Lotte Hattemer, one of the seven who signed at Munich, dies at Ascona in her twenties. She had walked out of a Berlin official's household and lived poor on the hill and off it. Rumour in the village puts a colony physician near the death; nothing was charged, and no source reached names a finding. Six years after the founding, one of the seven is dead and two are living outside the fence on ground of their own. The sanatorium receives guests through the season.
suggested_refs: The grave of Lotte Hattemer at Ascona, and the unresolved village rumour of 1906

stops.name: Monte Verita, Otto Gross comes for the cure
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1906 by the corpus file otto_gross.journey.json; the month is a placeholder
stops.campa: Otto Gross, psychoanalyst and morphine addict, climbs up to break his dependency on light, raw food and air. He is exactly the guest the tariff was written for and exactly the guest the doctrine cannot hold: he preaches free love to the household and finds Erich Muhsam and Johannes Nohl already there to hear it. Oedenkoven runs a sanatorium with a diet, a timetable and a fee, and it keeps filling up with people who want the mountain to be something else. What he made of the analyst at his own dining table is nowhere in the record.
suggested_refs: Otto Gross's Ascona cure of 1906 and the circle around Muhsam and Johannes Nohl

stops.name: Monte Verita, Hermann Hesse climbs up
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 1907 by the corpus files hermann_hesse.journey.json and ida_hoffmann.journey.json; the day is a placeholder
stops.campa: Hermann Hesse comes up in April from a cure at Locarno, drinking too much and writing too little, and takes the vegetarian regime for a stretch. He does not stay and he does not convert; he keeps what he wants from the hill and leaves the rest, which is what most of the guests do. The Ticino holds him anyway, and a dozen years later he settles a valley away for good. Photographs from that April put him on the terraces beside Oedenkoven and Hofmann, bearded and very thin.
suggested_refs: Photographs of Hermann Hesse at Monte Verita with Oedenkoven and Hofmann, April 1907

stops.name: Anacapri, the visit to Diefenbach
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: no independently fetched source confirms the visit or its date, which is carried only from earlier secondary compilation, and 1908 orders the segment. Coordinates corrected to Anacapri and the Villa Giulia, Diefenbach's actual house (en.wikipedia, 'Karl Wilhelm Diefenbach'); the Casa Rossa named in earlier compilation is a different building, built by John Clay MacKowen, with no Diefenbach association
stops.campa: On Capri, in the Villa Giulia at Anacapri, Karl Wilhelm Diefenbach has lived since 1899 in a robe and sandals, painting enormous symbolist canvases and refusing meat: the senior figure of German life reform, and the man who taught Gusto Graser to dress as he does. Oedenkoven and Hofmann are said to have gone to see him. The visit is carried only in secondary compilation. Diefenbach dies on the island in 1913, and his pictures end up in the Certosa di San Giacomo.
suggested_refs: Karl Wilhelm Diefenbach's Villa Giulia at Anacapri, and his paintings in the Certosa di San Giacomo

stops.name: Monte Verita, Villa Semiramis
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1909 with Anselmo Secondo as architect (monteverita.org/history); month and day are placeholders. The recollection quoted is verbatim from a page that was fetched, but its author is not named there and the underlying memoir or letter is untraced
stops.campa: The Turinese architect Anselmo Secondo puts up a guest house on the hill in a Piedmontese Jugendstil with triangular shutters and calls it Villa Semiramis. This is the sanatorium turning into a hotel in stone: more beds, better rooms, a tariff to match, guests who arrive by boat across the lake with luggage. They are cured of meat by daylight. A period recollection has them slipping down to the village after dark for salami and wine, and the proprietor patrolling for the evidence.
stops.quote: We had some guests sneak out, under cover of dark summer nights, to a nearby village to enjoy forbidden things like spiced salami and good local wine. Henri Oedenkoven kept finding the telltale rind of the rich local ewe's cheese. He would hold up the evidence between two fingers as if it was poison.
stops.quote_source: Period first-person recollection quoted, without attribution to a named author, in 'Monte Verita: The Swiss early hippie colony', aboutswitzerland.eda.admin.ch (Presence Switzerland); the underlying memoir or letter is not identified there
suggested_refs: Villa Semiramis, Monte Verita, by Anselmo Secondo of Turin, 1909

stops.name: Monte Verita, Laban's dance farm
stops.date_confidence: attested to summer 1913 (mediaguide.monteverita.org/en/the-history/1913-1918; corpus ida_hoffmann.journey.json and laban.journey.json); the day is a placeholder
stops.campa: Rudolf von Laban opens a school for art on the hill in the summer, on ground that belongs to Oedenkoven and Hofmann, and brings Mary Wigman with him. The sanatorium's own doctrine was diet, sun and cold water, a therapy for the sick; what the tenants practise is a discipline for the well. From this summer the hill carries two settlements at once, on one owner's ground. On the meadow above the terraces the dancers work barefoot through the whole season, moving to no music at all.
suggested_refs: Rudolf von Laban's Schule fur Kunst on Monte Verita, summer 1913

segments.name: The War Years on the Mountain, 1914-1918

stops.name: Monte Verita, the sessions of the order
stops.date_confidence: attested: HDS (hls-dhs-dss.ch, article 049204) states that Oedenkoven took part in sessions of the Ordo Templi Orientis from 1914 onward. No month, no day, and no account of what he did or believed there was located in any source reached
stops.campa: The Swiss dictionary records that from 1914 he takes part in sessions of the Ordo Templi Orientis. The director of a vegetarian sanatorium, a man of no confession who has spent fourteen years arguing that a body heals itself in sunlight, sits down in a lodge of degrees, oaths and secret rites. The hill has drawn theosophists since before he bought it; Pioda meant it for a lay monastery. What Oedenkoven thought he was doing in that room is nowhere on record.
suggested_refs: O.T.O. records for the Monte Verita lodge from 1914, unlocated

stops.name: Ascona, the war scatters the colony
stops.date_confidence: attested to August 1914 by the corpus files ida_hoffmann.journey.json and suzanne_perrottet.journey.json; the day is a placeholder
stops.campa: In August the guests become enemy nationals of one another: Germans, Austrians, Belgians and Russians at the same table, then gone. Switzerland is neutral and Ascona is a border village. The house empties inside a week. Oedenkoven and Hofmann keep it open anyway through four years of shut frontiers and money that will not cross them, taking whoever can still reach the hill. He is a Belgian citizen and his country is under occupation for the duration.
suggested_refs: The Monte Verita guest registers for 1914-1918, the war years of the sanatorium

stops.name: Monte Verita, Isabelle Adderley
stops.date_confidence: attested to the war years by de.wikipedia, 'Henri Oedenkoven', and the corpus file ida_hoffmann.journey.json; no source reached gives a month, a marriage date or the children's names, and 1916 orders the segment
stops.campa: An English dancer born in India, Isabelle Adderley, appears in the circle around the dance school. The reform marriage of 1900 had refused priest and registry as impositions laid on a free union. It now ends as a conjugal matter and continues as a household one: Ida Hofmann stays on under the same roof while Oedenkoven takes up with Adderley, whom he will marry in law, before a registrar. They have three children. No source reached gives the wedding date, the year of the break, or the children's names.

stops.name: Monte Verita, the Anational Congress
stops.date_confidence: attested to 15-25 August 1917 (en.wikipedia, 'Theodor Reuss'; mediaguide.monteverita.org/en/the-history/1913-1918). The date given is the opening day
stops.campa: Theodor Reuss, who has founded a lodge on the hill called Verita Mistica, holds his Anational Congress for the reconstruction of society on cooperative lines from the fifteenth to the twenty-fifth of August. There are sessions on cooperation, on women, on education, on esoteric themes. Oedenkoven, in the fourth year of a war that has emptied his rooms, lets it go ahead and takes the bookings. It closes with a ritual dance to the sun, kept up on the terraces from sunset until sunrise.
suggested_refs: The Anational Congress for Organising the Reconstruction of Society on Practical Cooperative Lines, Monte Verita, 15-25 August 1917

stops.name: Casa Anatta, Theodor Reuss put out
stops.date_confidence: disputed and not resolved here. en.wikipedia, 'Monte Verita', has Oedenkoven throw Reuss out promptly over objectionable midnight rituals; en.wikipedia, 'Theodor Reuss', has Reuss resident and hosting his congress in August 1917 and leaving some time before November 1918, with no cause given; HDS 049204 has Oedenkoven himself attending O.T.O. sessions from 1914. The expulsion therefore cannot be dated to 1917 as earlier compilation had it, and 1918-06 is a placeholder inside the only window both accounts leave open
stops.campa: He finds out what is being done at midnight in the name of the order and puts Reuss off the property, calling him a charlatan and a devourer of women. It is the second banishment the hill has pronounced, after Gusto Graser's, and the same man pronounces both. The chronologies disagree about when. One account has the expulsion prompt and immediate; another has Reuss still resident and hosting through 1917 and simply gone before November 1918, with no cause given at all.
stops.quote: a charlatan and devourer of women
stops.quote_source: Henri Oedenkoven on Theodor Reuss, as reported in the English Wikipedia article 'Monte Verita'
suggested_refs: Oedenkoven's correspondence on the closure of the O.T.O. working at Monte Verita, unlocated

stops.name: Monte Verita, the sale and the departure
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1920 (de.wikipedia, 'Henri Oedenkoven'; en.wikipedia, 'Monte Verita'; literaturkritik.de/id/6486). No source reached is more precise than the year: the 'January 1920' of earlier compilation is not supported, and the month here is a placeholder
stops.campa: Twenty years after the purchase he stops running the sanatorium and goes off the hill: Oedenkoven, Isabelle Adderley, their children, and Ida Hofmann, leaving together much as they had arrived together. Behind them are a working business, a set of buildings and a name known across Europe, and no successor out of the founding seven. Nothing more precise than the year survives, and nothing puts him on the hill again. The vegetarian cure does not resume on this ground.

stops.name: Spain, the attempt that left no address

No source reached names a Spanish province, town, purchase, date or outcome. The coordinate is a country-level placeholder for Spain and is not a claim that he was in Madrid; the date orders the segment
stops.campa: Between Switzerland and Brazil the party tries Spain. The Swiss dictionary says only that he attempted to establish vegetarian colonies in Spain and in Brazil, and that is the whole of the record: no province, no town, no purchase, no year, no outcome. Spanish land and colony papers for the Oedenkoven party were not located. He is forty-five, with a wife, three children, a former partner still in the household and twenty years of proof that the thing can be made to work, and he is looking for ground a second time.

stops.name: Monte Verita, the deed passes
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1923 for the transfer to the Berlin group (de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verita': Werner Ackermann, Max Bethke and Hugo Wilkens); it.wikipedia lists four, adding William Werner, and earlier compilation omitted Bethke entirely. Month and day are placeholders. The Canton Ticino page cited for this transfer in earlier compilation was fetched and does not contain the sentence attributed to it
stops.campa: Three years after he walks off it, the property is legally made over to a group out of Berlin, Werner Ackermann, Max Bethke and Hugo Wilkens, who mean to run it as a hotel for artists. By then Oedenkoven is on another continent. Somewhere in the same stretch a lease as a children's home fails; the artists' hotel fails too. In 1926 the banker Eduard von der Heydt buys the hill for a hundred and sixty thousand francs. The Italian account names a fourth man in the Berlin group, William Werner; the German account does not.
suggested_refs: The 1923 conveyance of Monte Verita to the Berlin group of Ackermann, Bethke and Wilkens

stops.name: Palmital, Santa Catarina: the colony called Monte Sol
stops.date_confidence: attested to a range, not a year: the SciELO study (Historia, Ciencias, Saude-Manguinhos, 'Em busca do novo Eden no seculo XX') says Monte Sol began sometime between 1921 and 1923, two decades after the Swiss colony, and attributes the founding to Ida Hofmann. The pin is the corpus's placeholder coordinate for the Brazilian colony, inherited from ida_hoffmann.journey.json; the region named by the source is Palmital in Santa Catarina and the exact site is unlocated. 'Near Joinville', carried in earlier compilation, appears nowhere in the source
stops.campa: In the Palmital region of Santa Catarina the household begins again and names the place Monte Sol, mountain of the sun: the second half of the first name, in another language. Natural healing in an attractive setting, the same offer as Ascona, transplanted into subtropical forest by people who do not know the country. The Brazilian scholarship gives the founding to Ida Hofmann and puts it two decades after the Swiss colony. The land they buy turns out to be unhealthy.
stops.quote: Ida Hofmann ended up establishing another colony, Monte Sol, in the Palmital region of Santa Catarina, Brazil.
stops.quote_source: SciELO, Historia, Ciencias, Saude-Manguinhos, 'Em busca do novo Eden no seculo XX: os portugueses e a fundacao de colonias naturistas no Brasil', English edition, scielo.br/j/hcsm/a/RgVCMBwGNWNzvWMwqKgV8nb

stops.name: Palmital, the colony fails
stops.date_confidence: the four-year duration and the two causes are verbatim from the SciELO study; the end date is a range, not a year. With a start between 1921 and 1923 the collapse falls c.1925-1927, and Ida Hofmann's death at Sao Paulo on 12 July 1926 brackets it. The pin is the corpus's Brazilian placeholder coordinate
stops.campa: It lasts about four years. The peer-reviewed account gives two causes and no others: the property acquired, which proved relatively insalubrious, and the way of life of the people who went there to live. The second is the fracture that emptied Ascona of half its founders in fourteen months, and this time there is no Belgian money underneath it to absorb the shock. Ida Hofmann dies at Sao Paulo on the twelfth of July 1926, in her sixties. The end of the colony is given as a range and not as a year.
suggested_refs: Simone Christol's study of Brazilian naturist colonies, cited in the SciELO article

stops.name: Catalao, Goias: the last attempt
stops.date_confidence: attested to the decade only: the SciELO study gives 'a new attempt in the municipality of Catalao, Goias, in the 1930s'. The year 1930 orders the segment and is not a record; earlier compilation's flat '1930' is not supported
stops.campa: There is one attempt more, in the 1930s, at Catalao in Goias, far inland on the high plateau where the cerrado runs to the horizon and the nearest railhead is a day away. It fails as well, and the Ticino hill is half a world behind him now. What he did there, who went with him, how long it lasted and what became of the land are recorded nowhere that could be reached: the Brazilian study gives a municipality and a decade and stops. He is in his late fifties, on his fourth site in thirty years.

stops.name: Sao Paulo, the death without a date
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year and the city, double-sourced (HDS, hls-dhs-dss.ch article 049204, by Andreas Schwab, 2009; de.wikipedia, 'Henri Oedenkoven'), and upgraded from the reconstruction status carried in earlier compilation, which had treated HDS as unreachable. stops.campa: He dies in 1935 at Sao Paulo, about sixty years old. The Swiss dictionary gives the year and the city and nothing further: no day, no cause, no address, no burial. His age at death is itself an estimate, the birth year being as bare as this one. Ida Hofmann had died in the same city nine years before him, which is the one thing that gives the location any weight, since it puts the emigrant household demonstrably in Sao Paulo. The civil death registers for 1935 were not consulted, and no grave has been found for either of them.

stops.name: Monte Verita, von der Heydt buys the hill
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1926 by de.wikipedia, it.wikipedia and monteverita.org, with the price of 160,000 francs from de.wikipedia; aboutswitzerland.eda.admin.ch dissents, giving 1927 for the purchase and 1928 for the hotel. The conflict is flagged and not resolved: 1926 has three backers and leads. The Fahrenkamp hotel is dated 1929 by de.wikipedia. Month and day are placeholders
stops.campa: The banker and collector Eduard von der Heydt buys the hill for a hundred and sixty thousand francs and turns Casa Anatta into a private house for his East Asian art. He approaches Mies van der Rohe for a new hotel and builds it with Emil Fahrenkamp instead: flat roofs, white walls, a modernist box set on the terraces the founders cleared by hand. What visitors come to see at Monte Verita from now on is the banker's building. The Swiss federal account dissents on the year, giving 1927 for the purchase and 1928 for the hotel.

stops.name: Monte Verita, Casa Centrale pulled down
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1948, verbatim from monteverita.org/history: demolished to make way for a restaurant, with only the curving flight of steps remaining. The '1904, commissioned by Oedenkoven' gloss carried in earlier compilation is not on that page and is not reproduced. Month and day are placeholders
stops.campa: The communal house with the yin and yang worked into its windows comes down to make room for a restaurant. The rooms where the household dined and read and held its assemblies, where Hofmann played and the guests argued through the evenings, go under the machines in a season. The site's own history dates the demolition to 1948 and records that one thing survives it. The curving flight of steps that went up to the door is left standing in the grass, going nowhere now, with nothing written on it.
stops.quote: In 1948 this building was demolished to make way for a restaurant and only the curving flight of steps remains
stops.quote_source: Fondazione Monte Verita, monteverita.org/history, on Casa Centrale

stops.name: Monte Verita, the hill without a grave
stops.date_confidence: attested as a positive confirmation of an absence: the commemorative-structures section of de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verita', was read directly and Oedenkoven appears nowhere on it. The date is that of the Arp sculpture and orders the stop; no grave, plaque or headstone for Oedenkoven has been located here or in Brazil
stops.campa: The hill accumulates memorials to other people. Elisar von Kupffer's pavilion goes up on the old solarium's foundation to hold his round painting of the blessed; Hans Arp's Roue Oriflamme is set on the grounds in 1962. Neither is for Oedenkoven, who bought the ground both stand on. There is no plaque, no bust, no headstone and no known grave for him, here or at Sao Paulo. The list of commemorative structures kept for the site was read through line by line, and his name is not on it anywhere.
suggested_refs: Hans Arp, Roue Oriflamme, Monte Verita, 1962; the Elisarion pavilion 'Chiaro mondo dei beati'

stops.name: Casa Anatta, the museum
stops.date_confidence: attested: reactivated in 1979 for the Monte Verita exhibition and the site's History Museum since 1981 (monteverita.org/history); the 1978 Ascona exhibition travelled to Zurich, Berlin, Munich and Vienna (de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verita'). Month and day are placeholders
stops.campa: His own house is opened again in 1979 to hold Harald Szeemann's exhibition on the mountain of truth, which goes on afterwards to Zurich, Berlin, Munich and Vienna and puts the colony back into general circulation. Since 1981 Casa Anatta has been the site's history museum. The double timber walls, the sliding partitions and the domed ceilings he designed to live inside now hold the record of the living that was done in them, in vitrines, with labels.
